row.title: Does what the model does (backing down, declining) add to its stated confidence in predicting its mistakes?
row.odds_reason: Rows literature 0.07, model 0.17, said-vs-did 0/2. Dry run passes only at odds ratio about 7.4, Haiku and Sonnet must both pass, and Smolin-Wilder found violations under 5%.
row.scoring_note: Rule 15: a re-analysis of wave 1's raw data (sv-said, sv-b1, sv-b2 caches) with no new data; sv-b2 is the first scored bet on that run.
row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is power: at these item counts the rule sees only a strong signal (odds ratio about 7), so a moderate one, like Yamin et al.'s 5–15%, reads as fail.
row.prior_work: **Mixed, straddling the bar.** Yamin et al. 2026 (arXiv 2602.06286; GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1, Llama-4 Scout; clinical tasks; belief and action in separate context windows) rejected sufficiency in all 16 cells. Adding the deferral action improved prediction of the true label by 6.15, 4.89, 5.11 and 15.19% (random-forest MSE, not log-loss). Smolin and Wilder 2026 (arXiv 2609.07943) found outcome-sufficiency violations under 5% (relative) for capable models, which predicts a miss at this bar. Feng et al. 2024 (arXiv 2402.00367) found abstaining when swayed beats thresholding verbal confidence. None of them tests a Claude model, a pushback action, or the trivia flag as a rival carrier. **What this bet adds:** current Claude models, two self-directed actions (backing down and declining), and a base model that already holds the one-bit item-type guess, so an action counts only for what it adds beyond the number *and* the type. The odds (0.10) sit below Yamin's range on purpose: that range is in another metric, our bar needs two models at once, and the committed dry run sees only a strong signal (§5). The re-scout of 2026-11-05 (`map/reads/prior-work-2026-11-05-sv8-sv12.md`) is checking these numbers in parallel; anything it changes goes to the design review, never into this frozen row.

row.lesson: "Correcting P16, P3 and P12: the trivia bit drove declining directly, unmodelled in dry runs. This bet puts the one-bit trivia flag in the base model and every dry-run world, whose P(pass) is 0.40–0.55 at a strong signal and 0 at none, and its odds are 10% (from 30% on the map) because Haiku and Sonnet must both pass."
row.design_change: the one-bit SimpleQA flag is in the base model ([1, u, t] vs [1, u, t, b]) so an action counts only beyond the number and the item type (P16, P3); every dry-run world lets the flag act directly on wrongness (none, OR 2.5, OR 5) and on the behaviour (measured 52% vs 8%), committed as experiments/sv-b4-worlds.txt with P(pass) 0.40-0.55 at OR 7.4 and 0-0.01 at none or OR 2.7 (P12); Sean's card event without the flag is a reported secondary
